excerpt: With the REST API, you can read, create, and update nearly everything in a workspace — pages, databases, users, comments, and more.
Personal access tokens (PATs) are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, Workers, and tools that should act as one Notion user.
Connections can subscribe to real-time events — like page updates, property changes, and new comments — via webhooks.
Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication... Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.

I'm always disappointed by note-taking tools calling themselves a Notion alternative when they do not provide database functionality like Notion. That's what makes Notion great.
I really appreciate how Notion is basically 'what if Google Docs but you can actually organize your information.' The collaborative components feel really powerful.
For a while I've been searching for a note app allowing multi-user editing, mobile access, and offline read-only viewing. For now I use Notion with hopes they implement offline mode eventually.

Notion feels like it's got serious range from individuals up to teams at large enterprises. It's incredibly flexible and configurable, and it was interesting to watch it eat away at things like Confluence over the years.
This is kinda weird, because I was happily giving them $4/month, and now I have no reason to keep giving them money since blocks limit was removed on free tier.
Notion is currently a jack of all trades and master of none. We tried using it as wiki, project tracker, issue tracker, CRM & spreadsheet, and quickly hit limits requiring manual maintenance.
Notion consuming 10-15% CPU while idle is a deal breaker to me. I wish they'd devote more resources to fix this (on macOS).
I love Notion, but the Mac client feels so sluggish—looks like a web view or Electron rather than a native Mac application.

Notion uses FullStory (session recording) for a note-taking app, which is a huge problem since potentially sensitive data is available to Notion/FullStory employees, and they don't disclose this upfront.
I had a really bad experience with Notion: hit an arbitrary 1000 block limit that no matter what I deleted I couldn't get rid of. Now I rely on vimwiki and fzf instead.
If I've understood it right, Notion is tied to its own cloud service for storing information, with no way to use it as standalone app storing data locally and syncing via my own service like Dropbox.

We switched to Notion after getting annoyed with Asana and not wanting to use Jira. We love how freeform it is and allowed us to create a workflow that fit us. Notifications are hit or miss though, and search still needs love.

I've started using Notion as a personal wiki and really like it—breaking the distinction between files and folders makes navigation easier than Google Docs. My only issue is it's hard to export/get stuff out, especially on mobile.

I use Notion for personal productivity and highly recommend it. It's one of the few personal tools I'm happy to pay for—like a personal wiki that makes it much easier to keep track of and refer back to old notes.

There is something about Notion that makes it feel very well-made and coherent, with really good real-time collaboration. On the flip side it's a bit slow to start and uses a lot of resources—it's based on Electron.

I love the product, but the login workflow is awful—a randomly-generated one-time code sent to email, unusable on my mobile device since I have no email on it. I really hope they implement traditional login.
I love Notion but the speed, or rather lack of it, is killing me daily. Last Friday I was taking notes and suddenly the page refreshed and everything was gone—I wasn't alone on Twitter.
Notion seems to be focused on wiki and notes, with built-in structured data allowing you to set up boards and task lists—it's a stretch to call a simple kanban tool a full Notion replacement.
As a heavy user of both Confluence and Notion: local/offline-first and mobile-first support is a big gap of Notion and ultimately why I had to ditch it.
My big problem with most document software including Notion: everything is locked in, hard to export/back up, and pricing is nickel-and-dimey—more nodes or people means upgrading tiers constantly.
